//: Glass Hours (docs/samples/Glass Hours.md — the app’s own sample film): its scenes, screenplay drafts, cast names and the eight location cards with the shared layouts the Art Room drafted for it (read-only copy, 2026-10-14). Used by test-location-false-openings.mjs and test-image-prompt-budget.mjs.

setting.period: present day, a winter of acqua alta
setting.location: a single family glass furnace on the Fondamenta dei Vetrai, Murano

styleBible.refs:
Glass Hours lives between two temperatures: the molten amber-orange of the furnace mouth and the cold pewter-green of flooded winter lagoon light, so every frame holds heat against damp and inheritance against loss. Light should feel handmade and finite. Furnace glow carves faces out of soot-dark workshop shadow, while grey acqua alta daylight seeps flat and wet through steamed, salt-streaked windows. Textures stay tactile and imperfect: crazed glass, scorched wood benches, wool and leather gone stiff with salt. The palette slowly warms as master and boy close the distance, then cools to the lehr's gentle annealing glow, a sense of something cooling slowly enough not to break.
Georges de La Tour — Single-source flame light raking across faces and hands, with deep umber falloff into darkness. Use it for furnace-mouth close-ups where the glory hole is the only light in the room.
Luca Bigazzi (cinematography of 'The Great Beauty' /… — Italian winter light that is luminous yet melancholic, with soft overcast diffusion over stone and water and a lingering, contemplative air in empty interiors.
Kodak Vision3 500T pushed one stop, 35mm — Visible organic grain that blooms in the warm highlights of molten glass, while shadows hold muddy green-black detail and nothing is digitally clean.
Edward Burtynsky / Mark Rothko colour fields — Restrained bands of burnt orange and ember red set against slate, lagoon jade and wet-stone grey. Keep warm saturation confined to the furnace zone and let everything else stay muted.

scenes.title: The Last Gather
scenes.summary: she takes a gather and opens it into a bowl at the master's bench, alone, counting in breaths. she lunges and makes the weld herself.

scenes.title: The Offer
scenes.summary: Luca arrives from Milan and sets a panettone on her ledger. he uncaps a pen on the contract and names Friday.
scenes.objective: to get her to sign the hotel's offer

scenes.title: The Boy at the Window
scenes.summary: Samir wipes his breath off the window and counts along with her. he tells her he saw the dawn bowl fall for lack of a second pair of hands.
scenes.objective: to get closer to the work

scenes.title: The Crack
scenes.summary: to fill an order, she turns the gas past her husband's pencil line on the dial. she says she will work small, glasses and beads.
scenes.objective: to keep the fire burning on her own terms

scenes.title: Terms
scenes.summary: Luca asks for time until Easter. without asking his mother, he writes the chandelier into the terms and initials it.
scenes.objective: to sell the furnace without selling his mother

scenes.title: Cullet
scenes.summary: Samir brings a fish crate of glass he hooked out of the canal at the stops. he unwraps the one shard he kept apart, in the family's gold-ruby red.

scenes.title: First Burn
scenes.summary: she makes him turn an empty pipe for ten minutes without stopping. she takes his hand, cools it and dresses it, and tells him about her husband's hands.
scenes.objective: to break him before he breaks something of hers

scenes.title: The Promise
scenes.summary: Luca hands her the hotel's chandelier specification, which reads "as agreed with L. Fiorin". he says she never lets anyone near that bench, and stops just before "me".
scenes.objective: to get her to accept the promise he made for her

scenes.title: Reticello
scenes.summary: she makes the first spiral cup and gives him the rule: every thread crosses another. she goes and sits by the window and leaves the glass to him.
scenes.objective: to teach him the net pattern before the month runs out

scenes.title: His Father's Bench
scenes.summary: Luca brings in the hotel's steel chandelier frame and the notary's date, and announces he got the price raised. the bucket when he was nine, and asking every Sunday until he was fourteen.
scenes.objective: to be welcomed as the son who saved them

scenes.title: Papers
scenes.summary: Samir comes in his best shirt with the burn hidden in his pocket. can he keep working at the furnace?
scenes.objective: to get papers without leaving the furnace

scenes.title: The Lehr
scenes.summary: a brick falls from the crown, and she orders every arm made tonight. when the hotel contract falls from his jacket, she tells him to go and carry their bags.
scenes.objective: to finish the chandelier before the furnace dies

scenes.title: The Canal
scenes.summary: Luca offers her Milan and the sunny room at the back. "I wanted it anyway. I still want it."
scenes.objective: to bring his mother home to Milan

scenes.title: The Staff Door
scenes.summary: Luca starts an apology for his mother that he can't finish. "No. She doesn't know I'm here."
scenes.objective: to bring Samir back to the furnace

scenes.title: Three at the Furnace
scenes.summary: she gives Samir the jacks and the red shard. He will make the heart, and she will hold. the chandelier in return for the crown, the furnace kept lit, and Samir on the hotel's books as an apprentice, with papers.
scenes.objective: to make the piece hold, and then give it away

scenes.title: The Second Bench
scenes.summary: Samir lets himself in with the keys and lights the new crown. he signs his own name on the base.
scenes.objective: to make and sign his first piece

blocks.text: Black. A roar. Then a mouth of fire, and out of it, on the end of a blowpipe, a ball of molten glass — swinging, turning, never still.
GRAZIELLA FIORIN (72), leather apron over a man's cardigan, walks it to the bench. Her lips move.
She sits at the scagno — the master's bench, its iron arms worn bright — and rolls the pipe along them. A pad of wet newspaper in her palm cups the glass. It opens into a bowl.
Beside her, a second bench. Nobody on it. On its arm, an espresso cup, poured. No steam.
The bowl begins to lean toward the floor.

She rests the pipe in the yoke, keeps it rolling with the flat of her left hand, and reaches with her right for the pontello heating in the furnace mouth. An arm's length too far. She stretches. Her shoulder clicks.
She looks at the second bench. At the cup.
She lunges, gets the iron, swings it to the bowl's base — but the glass has stiffened. The weld won't take.
The bowl tears off the pipe and bursts on the brick. A small, bright sound.
She sweeps the pieces into the cullet bin. One pass. Two.
Then she takes the cup from the empty bench and drinks the cold espresso in one swallow.
A cupboard of a room off the furnace floor. Ledgers, a gas bill under a glass paperweight, a bank calendar. Through the partition window, the furnace glows.
Graziella at the desk, reading glasses on.
LUCA FIORIN (34), good navy coat, trouser hems dark with seawater, sets a tall ribboned box on her ledger.
From Milan. The one you like.
She moves the panettone to the floor. As he sits, she touches his wet cuff. Once.
You walked through the acqua alta in those.
He slides the gas bill out from under the paperweight.
He lays a folder beside it, open at one line.
Two million one hundred thousand. A hotel group. Swedish.
What do Swedes want with fire? They have saunas.
There's a bowl in the cullet bin. This morning's.
You've never broken one in your life. Papà used to say —
Not by the door. The draught.
And keep that coat away from the furnace. You'll go back to Milan smelling of it.
He uncaps a pen and lays it across the folder.
They want an answer by Friday. I told them you'd at least —
She caps the pen. Closes the folder. Slides both back to him.
The four-ten gets you to Milan before dark.
You always knew the trains by heart.
He stands. Leaves the folder on the stool by the door. Goes.
Lamps coming on along the canal. A vaporetto shoulders past; its wash slaps the steps.
SAMIR HADDAD (19), a deckhand's waterproof, rope-roughened hands, stands at the furnace window. His breath fogs the glass. He wipes it with his cuff and leans in.
Inside, Graziella turns a pipe. His lips move with her count.
She feels it. Without looking up, she turns her stool until her back fills the window.
Samir steps to the next pane. Lifts his thermos and turns it slowly between his palms, in time with her.
The side door bangs open. Graziella, wiping her hands.
Every evening. You're counting my tools for somebody?
I finish at six. My boat is at twenty past.
He nods at the sacks of sand slumped by her door, dark with wet.
These are getting wet. I can carry them in —
Who sent you? The Swedes? My son?
He keeps his eyes on hers.
This morning, the first boat. I saw. You need somebody for the small iron. For the bottom.
Now go back to your boats.
She steps inside and hauls the shutter down over the window. Iron on stone.
Samir stands in front of it. Then he walks to the landing, his lips still moving.
Thirty goblets cooling on a rack, an order for a restaurant on Burano. Luca's folder on the stool by the door, a goblet foot on it for a paperweight.
Graziella at the gas valve. On the dial, a faded pencil line in a man's hand: 1150. She turns past it. The roar deepens. She works faster.
Across the furnace's domed crown, a seam of white light has opened in the brick.
ORESTE (78), the furnace mason, overcoat over pyjamas, taps a steel rod along the crown. A dead note. Further along. Dead.
I built this crown with Bepi. Ninety-eight. I know how she talks.
In ninety-eight it was one crack. Now she's tired all through. New crown, bricks from Germany, six weeks to dry.
I know what you sold. I drink with your accountant.
Then I work small. Glasses. Beads. Beads don't need a crown.
Oreste reaches past her and turns the valve down, well below Bepi's line. The roar sinks to a mutter.
At this she holds a month. Christmas, maybe. Then she comes down on whoever's under her.
Who's holding for you now, Graziella?
She crosses to the stool and lifts the goblet foot off Luca's folder. She doesn't open it. She doesn't step away from it.
Off-season. Dust sheets over half the armchairs. Beyond the windows, bathing huts shuttered against a grey Adriatic.
ANNIKA LUND (41), cashmere and reading glasses, turns a tablet toward Luca. His coffee is untouched.
She needs until spring. Easter. Let her finish the season.
I hear you. Look at this first.
On the tablet: the Fiorin furnace floor as a hotel lobby. The furnace kept, dark, behind a wall of glass, lit from below like a museum piece. A bar where the benches stand.
We keep the heart of it. A feature.
A feature. It won't be lit.
It can't be lit, Luca. The crown is cracked.
Murano is a small island. Her mason gave our surveyor a figure.
Two-point-one stands if we sign by the thirty-first. After that, we start again from the walls.
She still works. Every day. From dawn.
Then I'd like something she made. Over reception. A chandelier. Fiorin glass, under the Fiorin name.
Luca turns his cup a quarter turn on its saucer.
She'll make it. Put it in the terms.
Annika writes on the printed terms and initials it. He initials beside her: L.F.
The thirty-first, then. I'll send someone to measure on Thursday.
Low fire. The seam in the crown glows like a held breath.
On the brick beside the furnace mouth, someone else's yellow chalk: 2,40 × 1,80. An arrow. BAR? On the furnace door, a printed sticker: RETAIN — FEATURE.
Graziella scrubs the chalk with a wet rag. It smears to a yellow ghost and stays.
A knock. Samir in the doorway, a white fish crate in his arms, heavy with glass: bottle green, brown, one cobalt blue. Still dripping.
From the canal. I fish it at the stops, with the hook.
She picks out a green shard. Tosses it back.
Bottle. It doesn't marry with mine. It cracks.
I brought them. This afternoon, on the four-one. Two men and a laser.
points at the floor under her feet
They said the bar goes there.
She scrubs harder. The ghost spreads.
After my last boat, until the first one, I can work here. For nothing.
Nobody works for nothing. One day they want something.
She shoves the crate back over the threshold with her boot. It tips. Glass skates across the wet stones.
Samir kneels and gathers it back, piece by piece. From inside his jacket he takes a folded handkerchief. One shard, kept apart. A deep red, struck with gold.
She takes it to the furnace light. Turns it.
She closes her hand on it. Four breaths.
Samir at the second bench in gloves worn through at the fingers. An empty blowpipe across the iron arms.
Turn it. Don't stop till I say.
He rolls it along the arms. She sits with her coffee and watches the clock above the lehr. Ten minutes. His forearms shake.
She takes a gather from the furnace on a second pipe and swaps it into his hands. Fire, a hand's breadth from his face.
Now it's real. Turn. Never stop.
The gather stays round. She circles him once.
Choke up. Hands closer to the glass.
He slides his hands down the pipe, toward the end where the iron has drunk the heat. A hiss. Singed wool.
His jaw locks. He keeps turning. The gather stays round.
She lets him go four breaths. Five.
She takes the pipe and sets the piece in the lehr. Then she takes his wrist and pushes his hand into the quench bucket. Holds it there.
He looks at her hands. Old burns, white, on both palms.
She wraps his hand in a clean rag, slowly.
My husband's hands were like the bottom of a pan. He could hold a cup straight from the machine.
At the end he couldn't feel one at all.
Forty-one years he held for me. He never let one drop.
Grey daylight. On the marver, two espresso cups, both drained. On the second bench, a pair of scorched gloves.
Luca in his coat. Graziella holds a printed sheet at arm's length.
INSERT — THE SHEET: LJUSA HOTELS · MURANO HOUSE · RECEPTION CHANDELIER, Ø 140 CM, FIORIN GLASS. INSTALLED BY 31.12. AS AGREED WITH L. FIORIN. Initials: L.F.
She reads it twice. Lays it on the marver, very flat.
They want your name over their door. People will come to Murano for it.
A hundred and forty centimetres. At low fire, with that crown. You dropped a bowl on your own.
She lifts one of the two cups and turns it so he can see the coffee ring inside. He looks at the gloves on the second bench. At the scorch marks.
You don't let anyone near that bench. You never once let —
She holds out her hand. He doesn't understand. She takes the pen from his breast pocket.
One clean line through AS AGREED WITH L. FIORIN. Under it, in careful schoolroom script:
INSERT — THE SHEET: MADE BY G. FIORIN AND S. HADDAD. NOTHING IS SIGNED UNTIL IT HANGS.
She caps the pen, puts it back in his pocket, hands him the sheet.
Tell your Swedes they'll have their chandelier.
She turns to the furnace and opens the valve, up to Bepi's line and no further.
Samir's right hand in a fat white bandage.
Graziella lays thin white canes side by side in a ribbed mould, like matches in a box. She picks them up on a gather and twists: a cup striped in a slow white spiral.
Now one the other way. One inside the other. Every thread crosses another.
Samir's cup twists the other way: fast, eager, three turns too many. The threads bunch into a knot.
The bandage smaller. Over the surveyor's yellow ghost, Graziella chalks a net: lines crossing lines.
Not one of them lies alone.
Samir nods hard. Then he tries his own way, pinching two hot threads together quick, like a splice on a mooring line.
The cup folds in on itself with a soft sigh.
Graziella studies the ceiling for some time.
Four breaths before you touch it. Glass forgets slowly. Let it forget.
Glass forgets slowly. Let it forget.
A sticking plaster on his palm now.
Graziella sets her tools down, goes and sits on the stool by the window, hands in her cardigan pockets. Says nothing.
Samir alone with the two cups. He waits four breaths. Lowers one into the other. Blows.
The threads cross. Where every two meet, a tiny bubble of air is caught: a bead of light in each diamond of the net.
He holds it up, not breathing.
Each little bubble. That's your breath. In there for good.
The door swings open on the canal. A cargo boat at the steps, LJUSA on its tarpaulin. Two porters walk in a long crate.
Luca follows, flushed from the cold, an envelope under his arm. He prises the lid with a claw hammer. In foam: a steel chandelier frame, powder-coated black, LJUSA stamped on the ring.
They sent the bones. You fill them.
Notary, the thirty-first. And I got them to two-three. Two million three hundred. For your glass.
at the furnace mouth, not turning
Shut the door. You're letting out the heat.
He shuts it. Walks onto the floor in his good coat, into the heat, past the marver, and stops.
Samir at the second bench, turning a gather, a pair of worn steel jacks in his bandaged hand.
Luca looks at the jacks. The tape on one grip gone the colour of tea.
She said use them. They're the right weight.
It's a bench. It had nobody on it.
Luca looks at the quench bucket beside the bench.
I picked those up once. I was nine. You put my hands in that bucket and held them there.
I asked you every Sunday till I was fourteen. Then I stopped asking.
Her back stays turned. The fire on her face.
Luca lays the notary's envelope on the hotel's steel ring and goes. The door stays open on the cold.
INT. HOTEL STAFF CORRIDOR, LIDO — DAY
Behind the hotel's quiet front: strip lights, linen carts, a time clock, a noticeboard in five languages. Housekeepers pass in pairs, talking Tagalog, Bengali, Venetian.
Samir by the vending machine, his deckhand's waterproof over his best shirt. Right hand in his pocket.
Annika comes down the corridor with two paper cups.
You wrote to the boat depot. For me.
Your name was on a chandelier. I like to know who makes things for us.
She gives him a coffee. Then a plastic badge, already printed: SAMIR — GUEST SERVICES.
A real contract? For the Questura?
Permanent. We sponsor the permit, our lawyer does the forms. Papers by the summer.
He breathes out. Almost a laugh.
When the Murano house opens. In the spring.
The contract is for that hotel.
He understands a second after she says it. That house opens only if the furnace is sold.
And the fornace? I can still work at the fornace?
You'll be in that building every day. You'll walk past it.
She's taught you to carry glass without dropping it. That's most of this job.
On the boat I carry things already.
She holds out a pen. He doesn't take it. He folds the contract in four and buttons it inside his jacket.
Behind him a housekeeper punches the time clock. Clack.
The chandelier nearly made. On the hotel's black frame, nine reticello arms catch the fire, every thread crossed. On the marver, the great bowl of its heart, waiting.
A crack overhead. A brick drops out of the crown into the furnace mouth. Sparks skitter across the floor.
All of it tonight. Every arm.
Samir works. Quiet. His jacket on the hook by the door, a corner of white paper at its breast.
She goes to the lehr's controller. A curve on its panel: 48 H. She thumbs it down. 12 H.
He loads them: the arms, the heart. Shuts the lehr. Then he sits on the second bench with his back to her.
Grey at the windows. She opens the lehr. Heat rolls out. She lifts the heart onto the marver.
A line runs through the heart like a hair. Another ping, an arm. Another.
Samir reaches for his jacket. His first boat. The paper slides out onto the brick.
She picks it up. The letterhead. GUEST SERVICES.
He takes the paper back from her, gently. Lays the jacks on the second bench, square to its edge, the way she keeps them. Goes.
Graziella alone with the cracked heart. The second bench empty again.
The acqua alta siren: rising tones across the lagoon. The canal has come up over the stones; the fondamenta is a sheet of black water holding the furnace's red.
Graziella in rubber boots, a crate of cracked glass in her arms, wades toward the cullet skip at the water's edge.
Luca along the fondamenta in his Milan shoes. He doesn't stop at the water. He walks in.
It's over. You sign on the thirty-first and you come to Milan. The room at the back gets the sun.
He takes the other end of the crate. She lets him.
They carry it together, slowly, the water at their ankles, and set it on the lip of the skip.
You gave a boy off the boats Papà's bench.
She lifts the cracked heart out of the crate. Holds it between them.
You were nine. You picked his jacks straight out of the fire. I saw the skin come off your fingers, and I saw your father's hands on you.
Every winter we owed for the gas. I wanted you to have hands that could feel a cup.
The siren stops. Only the water, lapping.
She looks at his hand on the crate. Takes it. Turns it over. A soft palm. She runs her thumb across it.
She lets the cracked heart slide into the skip. Luca looks out across the lagoon, to the lights of the Lido.
EXT. HOTEL STAFF ENTRANCE, LIDO — DAWN
Bins, a gull on one lid. A laundry boat backing off the service landing. The staff door: a keypad, a buzzer.
Samir on an upturned crate in a borrowed porter's jacket, a roll of bread in one hand, the folded contract in the other. A badge on his lapel.
Luca comes up from the landing, unshaven, last night's water still in his shoes.
She didn't mean it. She doesn't — I'm sor —
Seven o'clock. I sign at seven.
There's a lawyer in Milan. Permits, it's all he does. I'll pay him.
She has a paper for me. They have a paper for me. Now you have a paper for me.
Luca sits on the next crate. Holds out his hands, palms up.
Look at these. I've never once held a pipe.
The heart is twelve kilos on the iron. She can't hold it up any more. I can't turn it. And you can't do both.
Samir looks at him a long moment. The keypad chirps; the staff door swings open on light and steam.
He unpins the badge and lays it on the crate, the contract on top. Pockets the bread. Walks toward the landing.
The five-one goes at ten past.
Luca gets up and follows him.
Low red light. The hotel's black frame, bare. Graziella on the master's bench, not working.
The door. Samir. Behind him, Luca.
Nobody speaks. She holds out the jacks. Samir takes them. Then the red shard, set in his palm, on the scar.
In the first gather. You make the heart. I hold.
The fire up, to Bepi's line and no further.
Samir gathers, the red melting into the glow like a thread of wine in honey. Again. Again. The heart swells on the pipe.
Luca's hands, either side of the pipe on the yoke, steady it. He doesn't let go.
Graziella brings the pontello to its base. The weld takes.
She sets the lehr's curve: 48 H. Sits on the second bench.
Fireworks tested over the lagoon. Annika in the doorway, a notary's folder under her arm.
I've come for your signature. And the keys.
Samir and Luca lift the heart from the lehr, a vein of gold-red through it. Samir taps it with a fingernail.
You hang it over your desk. You pay for the crown. The furnace stays lit, here, and he's on your books as an apprentice. With papers.
Stays a furnace. Your guests come and watch.
My son says they love a story.
Annika looks at Luca. He doesn't look away.
The signal's better on the fondamenta.
Annika steps out with her phone.
Graziella unhooks the furnace keys from her belt. One long breath. She puts them in Samir's burned hand.
MARCH. A new crown, its brick still pale.
A key in the lock. Samir lets himself in and lights the furnace. The roar.
On the marver, an opened envelope on hotel letterhead: CONTRATTO DI APPRENDISTATO — HADDAD, S. Beside it, two espresso cups. He fills both.
At the window, Graziella in her coat, no apron, peels an orange in one long ribbon. She doesn't look up.
Samir at the second bench. He gathers, rolls, blows. After every move his eyes go to her.
She holds out a segment of orange to Luca, who kneels on the brick with his phone, framing the bench.
Don't look at her. Look at the glass. You're in the light.
From the lehr Samir takes yesterday's piece: a small reticello cup, a bead of air in every diamond. He holds the diamond- point pen out to her, handle first.
Her hands stay in her coat pockets.
He waits. She eats a segment of orange.
He turns the cup over and scratches into the base, slowly: S. Haddad · Fornace Fiorin. The date.
Graziella picks up the second cup. The coffee is hot. She drinks.
Samir goes to the furnace for the next gather. She watches the second bench, her lips moving, counting without a sound.

spatialPlan.frame: DESIGN frame, no image supplied: standing just inside the main entrance door (A-door) of the Fiorin Furnace workshop, facing the far wall where the furnace (A-furnace) stands. 'Far' means toward the furnace and 'near' means toward the door. Frame-left and frame-right are as seen from this standpoint, and every placement is also tied to anchor IDs.

anchors.name: Main glory-hole furnace
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: 'a mouth of fire', 'The furnace answers.'
anchors.placement: Centred against the far wall, opposite A-door. A brick-clad body with one open, fire-lit working mouth (A-mouth) at roughly seated-to-standing working height, facing into the room toward A-door.

anchors.name: Furnace working mouth with pontello rest
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: pontello 'heating in the furnace mouth. An arm's length too far.'
anchors.placement: Opening in the near face of A-furnace. A pontello rest sits at its lip so the iron tip heats inside. The lip is slightly more than a seated arm's reach from the right side of A-scagno, so a seated reach falls short and a lunge succeeds.

anchors.name: Master's bench (scagno) with iron arms worn bright
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: scagno with iron arms worn bright; pipe rolled along them; right-hand reach goes toward the furnace mouth.
anchors.placement: On the brick floor, frame-left of A-mouth and a short distance nearer the door. Placed so the seated gaffer's RIGHT side faces A-mouth. Its two iron arms run toward and away from A-furnace. A-yoke stands at the arms' right-hand end, A-bench2 on the gaffer's left.

anchors.name: Pipe yoke (rest stand)
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: 'rests the pipe in the yoke, keeps it rolling with the flat of her left hand'.
anchors.placement: Freestanding iron yoke just past the right end of A-scagno's arms, between A-scagno and A-mouth. Holds the pipe while the seated gaffer rolls it with her left hand, freeing her right hand to reach toward A-mouth.

anchors.name: Second (assistant's) bench
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: 'Beside her, a second bench. Nobody on it. On its arm, an espresso cup'.
anchors.placement: Parallel to A-scagno, immediately on its frame-left, on the side away from A-mouth. It is within the seated master's eyeline. A cup is set on its near arm. It is the assistant's (Bepi's) station and stays empty in this scene.

anchors.name: Brick work floor
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: 'bursts on the brick'.
anchors.placement: Continuous brick floor across the work zone from A-mouth to A-door. The patch beneath and in front of A-yoke and A-scagno is where the bowl falls and shatters.

anchors.name: Cullet bin
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: 'sweeps the pieces into the cullet bin. One pass. Two.'
anchors.placement: Steel bin on A-floor, frame-left of A-bench2 or just behind A-scagno toward A-door. Close enough to sweep the shards into from the break zone in two passes, without moving away from the benches.

anchors.name: Water bucket for newspaper pads
anchors.evidence: No image. Implied only by the wet newspaper pad; its position is invented.
anchors.placement: Low bucket on A-floor beside the left leg of A-scagno, within reach of the seated gaffer.

anchors.name: Main entrance door
anchors.evidence: No image. Not in script.
anchors.placement: In the near wall, opposite A-furnace. It is the reference standpoint for the frame and opens toward the Murano fondamenta or calle.

anchors.name: High dawn window
anchors.evidence: No image. Script gives DAWN only; the window itself is invented.
anchors.placement: Set high in the frame-left side wall, above and behind A-bench2. It admits cool dawn light that contrasts with the orange glow from A-mouth on A-scagno.

anchors.name: Annealing oven (lehr)
anchors.evidence: No image. Not in script. Typical furnace dressing.
anchors.placement: Against the frame-right side wall, nearer A-door than A-furnace, frame-right of A-mouth. It is out of the bench working zone.

spatialPlan.sightlines: Single space with no subspaces. From A-door the view runs straight to A-furnace and A-mouth, with A-scagno, A-bench2 and A-cullet frame-left of A-mouth. From the seat of A-scagno, A-mouth lies to the gaffer's right and A-bench2 to her left, inside her eyeline. A-door, opposite A-furnace, is the only proposed opening to the exterior. A-window is a light source only, with no through-view established.
spatialPlan.unresolved: No reference image, so all geometry is design or script inference, not observed. Not yet decided: the scagno's exact angle to the furnace face, and whether the gaffer faces toward or away from A-door. Also open: furnace-mouth height and size, room dimensions, ceiling height and the walls the script does not mention. The existence and positions of A-door, A-window, A-annealer and A-bucket are proposals. Need confirmation of the exact reach distance from the seated master to the pontello for the stretch-and-lunge beat. Mouth heights and bench and yoke dimensions need real measurements; none have been invented. Awaiting human review before the first render.

spatialPlan.frame: DESIGN frame: stand on the threshold of the canal-side street door, facing into the furnace floor. 'Far wall' = opposite the street door. 'Left/right' = as seen from that threshold. The office is a partitioned corner room off the floor. No image was supplied. Every placement below is proposed for human review before the first render.

anchors.name: Canal-side street door and stone threshold
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: knock, Samir in doorway, crate shoved back over threshold, glass skates across wet stones.
anchors.placement: Centre of the near wall, opening onto the fondamenta. Wet stone floor runs inside. Source of the draught. Samir stands here, and the crate is shoved back over this threshold.

anchors.name: Glass furnace with domed brick crown
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: domed crown, crack seam of white light, mason taps crown.
anchors.placement: Centred against the far wall, facing street-door so its glow reads from the entrance. Its mouth faces the room centre. The crown is reachable by Oreste's rod from the floor.

anchors.name: Furnace mouth and door with RETAIN — FEATURE sticker
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: sticker on furnace door; chalk on brick beside furnace mouth.
anchors.placement: Front face of furnace, toward the room centre. Chalk brick (chalk-brick) sits immediately beside it. The sticker stays on the door from the late-night scene onward.

anchors.name: Yellow chalk '2,40 × 1,80 → BAR?' (later a smeared ghost)
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: chalk beside furnace mouth; arrow; scrubbed to a yellow ghost.
anchors.placement: Brickwork directly right of furnace-mouth-door at chest height. The arrow points down toward bar-spot. Once scrubbed, it stays as a yellow smear.

anchors.name: Gas valve with dial and pencil line '1150'
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: Graziella at gas valve; dial with faded pencil 1150; Oreste reaches past her.
anchors.placement: On the furnace's right flank or the far wall just right of the furnace, at hand height. The operator standing there faces the dial with the crown overhead.

anchors.name: Floor area marked for the proposed bar
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: Samir points at floor under her feet: 'the bar goes there'.
anchors.placement: Open floor between furnace-mouth-door and the room centre, where Graziella stands while scrubbing chalk-brick. It is not a physical object, just a continuity position.

anchors.name: Office partition wall with window
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: 'through the partition window, the furnace glows'; office is a cupboard of a room off the floor.
anchors.placement: Encloses the left-near corner of the floor, between street-door and the left wall. Its window faces the far wall so the office sees furnace glow.

anchors.name: Office doorway to furnace floor
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: 'Not by the door. The draught.' Luca leaves via door.
anchors.placement: In office-partition, on its right (room-facing) side, opening onto the floor near street-door. Graziella says sitting by it is draughty, so it is close to street-door.

anchors.name: Stool by the door (holds Luca's folder)
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: folder left on stool by the door (office scene) and still on stool by the door (furnace scene).
anchors.placement: On the floor side, against office-partition, just right of office-door and near street-door. The same stool is visible from inside the office through office-door and later on the floor at night.

anchors.name: Desk with ledgers, gas bill, glass paperweight
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: Graziella at desk; ledgers, gas bill under glass paperweight; Luca sits.
anchors.placement: Against office-partition under the window. Graziella sits facing the window and furnace. The visitor chair is on the office-door side.

anchors.name: Bank calendar
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: bank calendar listed in office dressing.
anchors.placement: On the office's solid back wall, behind the visitor chair, opposite the partition window.

anchors.name: Annealing lehr with wall clock above
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: 'the clock above the lehr'.
anchors.placement: Along the right wall, running from near the far wall toward the room centre. The clock is mounted on the wall above the lehr and is visible from the second-bench seat.

anchors.name: Cooling rack (thirty Burano goblets)
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: thirty goblets cooling on a rack.
anchors.placement: Against the right wall nearer street-door, at the outfeed end of lehr.

anchors.name: Main gaffer's bench with iron arms
anchors.evidence: No image. Script implies a first bench because a 'second bench' exists.
anchors.placement: Left of the room centre, side-on to furnace-mouth-door, about one stride's reach to the glory hole. Graziella's working position.

anchors.name: Second bench with iron arms
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: Samir at the second bench rolling a blowpipe on the iron arms.
anchors.placement: Right of the room centre, mirroring bench-main across the furnace mouth, facing lehr and its clock.

anchors.name: Cullet bin
anchors.evidence: No image. Script: Luca mentions 'a bowl in the cullet bin'.
anchors.placement: Left wall near the furnace, beside bench-main, within throwing reach of the working position.

spatialPlan.sightlines: Street-door view (design): the furnace glow is dead ahead on the far wall. The office partition, its window and office-door are on the left. The lehr, clock and goblet rack are on the right. Office view: through the partition window, Graziella at office-desk looks across the floor to furnace-mouth-door and the crown. Through office-door, door-stool and part of street-door are visible. From the gas-valve position, the crown is overhead and bar-spot is in front. From bench-second, the clock above lehr is visible.
spatialPlan.unresolved: No reference image; all placements are design proposals. No dimensions for the floor, office, furnace size or crown height. Chalk dimensions 2,40 × 1,80 are script text, not a measured room size. Ambiguity: 'stool by the door' appears in the office scene and on the furnace floor. Placing it on the floor side beside office-door is a reconciliation that needs approval; it could instead belong inside the office or at street-door. It is unclear which door causes the draught. Placement of the glory hole versus the melting furnace (a single structure is assumed). Lehr type and orientation. Whether the office has its own exterior window. The fourth wall of the office and the left wall of the floor are unseen and undefined. Whether the floor is level with or below street-door, given the acqua alta water.

spatialPlan.sightlines: From the quay facing north, fv-furnace-window reveals fv-furnace-bench and the glowing furnace mouth; once fv-window-shutter is down, the window shows only iron. Through fv-side-door, the furnace interior glow is glimpsed. Looking south from the façade, you see fv-canal-edge, fv-water-steps, fv-cullet-skip, passing vaporetti and the far canal bank. Looking south-east, f-lagoon-vista with the Lido lights. Looking east along the quay, f-lamp-row leads to f-vaporetto-landing. Looking west, the quay continues past other buildings. At night the flooded quay reflects the furnace red from the window.

coverageSheets.name: Hotel Staff Corridor Exterior
coverageSheets.summary: Exterior coverage required by the screenplay: the scene looks out from the interior or cuts to the outside of this place. Render the empty exterior/facade, approach, openings and sightline back toward the interior.
coverageSheets.scriptExcerpt: INT. HOTEL STAFF CORRIDOR, LIDO — DAY Behind the hotel's quiet front: strip lights, linen carts, a time clock, a noticeboard in five languages. Housekeepers pass in pairs, talking Tagalog, Bengali, Venetian. Samir by the vending machine, his deckhand's waterproof over his best shirt. Right hand in his pocket. Annika comes down the corridor with two paper cups. SAMIR You wrote to the boat depot. For me. ANNIKA Your name was on a chandelier. I like to know who makes things for us. ...
